skill.name: webask-quiz-logic
skill.description: Настраивает логику показа вопросов в опросе WebAsk — ветвление, пропуск блоков, отсев неподходящих респондентов и квоты. Применяется, когда человек хочет показывать разные вопросы разным людям или жалуется, что опрос ведёт респондента не туда.
skill.summary: Configure WebAsk survey branches, block skipping, respondent screening, and quotas using existing question identifiers.
skill.author: webaskio

content.value_statement: Incorrect survey routing can trap respondents or show irrelevant questions. This skill guides an assistant through reading WebAsk survey structure, updating conditions, and reviewing each route.
actual_capabilities: Read existing survey structure and question identifiers with get_quiz_structure before changing routing.
Configure answer-based branches and block skipping through update_quiz_logic.
Route ineligible respondents to a screenout destination and configure group quotas.
Apply question-type-compatible operators, first-match condition ordering, and Other-option selection rules.
Review routes for missing exits and backward loops, and describe complex branching in words.
limitations: Requires access to WebAsk MCP tools; this package does not implement those tools.
Works with existing questions and does not change the question set alongside routing.
Route review is instruction-based, not an included automated survey execution test.
Stops when service limits prevent changes and does not handle billing or plan upgrades.

use_cases.title: Route customer feedback
use_cases.description: Ask dissatisfied customers for details while letting other respondents skip irrelevant follow-up questions.

use_cases.title: Screen research participants
use_cases.description: Send ineligible respondents to a dedicated screenout and limit participation when a target group reaches its quota.

use_cases.title: Review existing survey routes
use_cases.description: Inspect condition ordering, branch exits, and backward transitions before making targeted routing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add a rating follow-up
prompt_templates.prompt: In WebAsk survey [survey], ask the existing follow-up question when the rating is below four. Read the structure first and describe the route.

prompt_templates.title: Skip an irrelevant block
prompt_templates.prompt: In WebAsk survey [survey], skip the service-quality block for respondents who did not use the service. Keep existing questions and check both routes.

prompt_templates.title: Set screening and a quota
prompt_templates.prompt: Read WebAsk survey [survey]. Route respondents failing [eligibility criteria] to screenout and cap [group] at [count] responses. Review condition order and exits.

prompt_templates.title: Repair complex routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect WebAsk survey [survey] for dead ends, backward loops, incompatible operators, and conflicting conditions. Explain proposed repairs, apply approved logic changes, and summarize every route.

output_examples.input: Show the existing explanation question only when the rating is below four.
output: Example route: ratings below four lead to the explanation question, then continue to the next block.
Ratings of four or higher skip the explanation question and continue to the same block.
Both routes have an exit without returning to an earlier question.

output_examples.input: Why does typing a particular word under Other not trigger my branch?
output_examples.output: The condition matches selection of the Other option, not the text entered beside it. Base the branch on that option selection.

output_examples.input: Screen out ineligible respondents and stop accepting a group after 200 responses.
output: Example route: respondents failing the eligibility condition go to the screenout destination.
Eligible respondents continue while their group remains below 200 responses.
Once the quota is reached, additional respondents from that group do not proceed.

best_practices: Read the current survey structure before every routing change and use the returned question identifiers.
Match operators to question types and order conditions carefully because the first matching condition wins.
Review every branch through completion and provide a written route map when branching becomes complex.
anti_patterns: Guessing question identifiers or writing routing rules without first reading the survey structure.
Changing survey questions and routing together, making failures harder to diagnose.
Creating backward transitions or branches without an explicit exit.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses get_quiz_structure to read a survey and update_quiz_logic to write routing changes through WebAsk MCP.

faq.question: Can it create new questions?
faq.answer: This skill focuses on existing survey routing. Its instructions explicitly separate question changes from logic changes.

faq.question: Can it configure screening and quotas?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes routing ineligible respondents to screenout and preventing further participation once a group quota is reached.

faq.question: Does Other match the text a respondent enters?
faq.answer: No. The documented condition matches the Other option itself, not the free text entered with it.

faq.question: Does it automatically test every survey path?
faq.answer: No automated test runner is included. The skill instructs the assistant to review each route from the first question through completion.

faq.question: What happens when a service limit blocks a change?
faq.answer: The assistant should explain the limit and stop. The skill instructs it not to suggest plan changes or direct users to payment.
